quiz_item.question: During a troop discussion on workplace rights for Requirement 1, a Scout asks why nineteenth and early twentieth century workers organized labor unions. Which explanation is historically accurate?
options: A. Workers organized primarily to abolish hourly wages in favor of unpaid agricultural apprenticeships and longer seven-day factory schedules.
B. Labor unions were created by railroad corporations to set nationwide retail prices and eliminate interstate freight tariffs.
C. Workers joined together to bargain collectively for safer working conditions, an eight-hour workday, fair living wages, and laws ending exploitative child labor.
D. Early unions were formed by federal courts to ban strikes and require employees to purchase their own heavy factory machinery.
choices: A. Workers organized primarily to abolish hourly wages in favor of unpaid agricultural apprenticeships and longer seven-day factory schedules.
B. Labor unions were created by railroad corporations to set nationwide retail prices and eliminate interstate freight tariffs.
C. Workers joined together to bargain collectively for safer working conditions, an eight-hour workday, fair living wages, and laws ending exploitative child labor.
D. Early unions were formed by federal courts to ban strikes and require employees to purchase their own heavy factory machinery.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Workers joined together to bargain collectively for safer working conditions, an eight-hour workday, fair living wages, and laws ending exploitative child labor.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The American labor movement arose so workers could use collective bargaining to address workplace hazards, excessive hours, low pay, and child labor.
